assessments.reasoning: The publisher's Haskell 2010 Language Report Chapter 5 resource is in the same edition and names Modules in its title and heading. The independently downloaded full response SHA-256 matches the registered source revision. Chapter 5's opening describes imports and exports. Section 5.2 explains omission and the default. Imports add resources to scope and exports expose available entities to other modules. A synthesized default is permitted. The document applies to language-level modules in Haskell 2010. A module can use implicit Prelude imports, omit export syntax, or include only its declared entities. Those cases preserve the import/export model.

limitations: An omitted export list has a documented default, so this description does not imply every module spells out an explicit list.
